articles.title: Netball Super League: Fixtures set for 2027 season with Netball Super Cup heading to Nottingham's Motorpoint Arena
articles.summary: Netball Super League contains 14 rounds of regular matches before play-offs and Grand Final; London Pulse won title in 2025 and AO Manchester Thunder beat Pulse in the 2026 Grand Final; The Netball Super Cup will take place on February 27 at Nottingham's Motorpoint Arena
articles.body:
Defending champions AO Thunder will get the season under way with a huge clash against Loughborough Lightning on Friday, March 5, with Nottingham Forest and Birmingham Panthers also set to go head-to-head on the opening night.

The Netball Super Cup is a one-day event each year created to showcase the eight Super League teams in the same place. For the first time since the Super Cup's inception in 2025 the showpiece occasion will go to Nottingham's Motorpoint Arena.

Last year's Netball Super Cup champions Loughborough Lightning, who missed out on a spot in the 2026 League final, are set to defend their title in front of a Midlands crowd as all eight clubs look for a strong start ahead of their 2027 League campaigns.

The 2027 season sees the return of double-header matches, with four set to take place across the campaign.

Netball Super League Competitions Director Ian Holloway said: "It's incredibly exciting to reveal our 2027 fixtures as momentum continues to build towards the third season of the new era of the Netball Super League.

"Over the past two years we've made a number of bold changes, and the incredible growth that our league has experienced since has demonstrated the power and potential that we know exists within our sport.

"We're continuing to provide bigger and better platforms for our inspirational female athletes to perform on, fuelling the growth of the league and ensuring netball remains firmly at the heart of the growth of women's sport."

articles.title: Glenn Irwin: Northern Ireland rider Irwin could ride at Brands Hatch after hospital discharge
articles.summary: Northern Ireland's Glenn Irwin is discharged from hospital after crashing in Sunday's British Superbike round at Donington Park.
articles.body:
Northern Ireland's Glenn Irwin has been discharged from hospital after crashing in Sunday's British Superbike round at Donington Park.

The 36-year-old was moved to Queen's Medical Centre in Nottingham after the incident because of "concern regarding a possible spinal fracture".

However, there was a positive update from the British Superbike Championship.

It said that Irwin been "pronounced clear and discharged and will be reviewed for fitness to ride at Brands Hatch".

Irwin crashed on the penultimate lap of the third BSB race of the weekend at Starkey's Bridge.

He was assessed and treated at the medial centre at the circuit, and was conscious and stable throughout.

It is the second time that the Ducati rider has been taken to hospital after a crash this season.

Irwin sustained pelvic and neck injuries in a crash at Snetterton in July and missed the two remaining races that weekend.

BSB leader Kyle Ryde won the opening two races of the weekend at Donington but Scott Redding clinched the third and final outing to take the championship to the final weekend at Brands Hatch from 17-18 October.

articles.title: “It was an honor when she asked to play”: How Caitlin Clark honored her cancer-survivor family friend and kept him close to her foundation
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark once replaced her famous last name with “Keough” on her Iowa jersey.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark once replaced her famous last name with “Keough” on her Iowa jersey. The name belonged to Dan Keough, a childhood family friend and cancer survivor. She wore it during Iowa’s Play 4 Kay game against Illinois on Feb. 25, 2024. Years later, Keough remains part of Clark’s world as a board member of the Caitlin Clark Foundation.Clark’s connection with Keough goes back to her childhood in Iowa. His son, Michael, played on the same second-grade team as Clark, and Keough helped coach the team. That early family friendship later became part of one of the most personal jersey tributes of Clark’s college career.Caitlin Clark chose Keough’s name during Iowa’s cancer awareness gameKeough’s connection to Clark became especially personal after he battled colorectal cancer in 2012. When Iowa played Illinois on February 25, 2024, the Hawkeyes took part in the Play 4 Kay game, which raises awareness and funds for breast cancer research. The players wore different names on their jerseys to honour people important to them.Clark chose “Keough.”The choice carried a personal link to her childhood. Keough had known Clark and her family since she was young, and his son Michael had played with her on a second-grade boys’ team. Keough also helped coach the group.Clark’s tribute came during a huge game for Iowa. The Hawkeyes beat Illinois 101-85, while Clark posted 24 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists for her sixth triple-double of the 2023-24 season. She finished the game with “Keough” on the back of her No. 22 jersey.Keough later explained what the moment meant to him in a February 27, 2024 interview with the University of Iowa’s Tippie College of Business. “As a cancer survivor, it was an honor when she asked to play with my name on her jersey,” he said while discussing his life, career and connection with Clark. He also said the tribute supported cancer awareness and survivorship.The gesture was not their first jersey connection. Keough also publicly acknowledged Clark wearing his name in February 2022, when he praised her competitiveness and positivity while linking those qualities to people fighting cancer. Keough now serves as a board member of Caitlin Clark’s FoundationKeough now holds a formal role as a board member of the Caitlin Clark Foundation. The Foundation says he brings business insight and a commitment to healthy living, while noting his longstanding relationship with Clark and her family.The Foundation focuses on three areas: education, nutrition and sports. Its work includes school-supply programs, youth sports facilities and food initiatives. It has also partnered with Scholastic on book programs and supports opportunities that help children learn, stay nourished and play.The Foundation has expanded its work in 2026 as well. In August, it launched its Turning Pages, Healing Hearts program at Blank Children’s Hospital in Des Moines, giving young patients books and activities during hospital stays. The program also launched earlier in August at Peyton Manning Children’s Hospital in Indianapolis.In Keough's case, his role on the board adds another chapter to a relationship that began on a second-grade basketball team. articles.title: Asian Games 2026: 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was India's youngest medallist; do you know who was the oldest?
articles.summary: The Asian Games 2026 took place in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from September 19 to October 4, with athletes from 46 nations competing across various sports.
articles.body: The Asian Games 2026 took place in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from September 19 to October 4, with athletes from 46 nations competing across various sports. India finished fourth in the medal table with 85 medals, including 21 golds, 27 silvers and 37 bronzes.India enjoyed several memorable performances, with the men’s and women’s teams winning gold medals in cricket, kabaddi and hockey. It was also the first time both Indian hockey teams won gold at the same Asian Games.Among the standout individual performers was 17-year-old archer Kumkum Mohod, who became the first Indian woman to win individual recurve gold.She finished the Games with two golds and a silver. Pranavi Urs also created history by winning India’s first individual golf gold, while Neeru Dhanda became the country’s first women’s trap shooting gold medallist.Vaibhav becomes India’s youngest medallistAt just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became India’s youngest-ever Asian Games gold medallist. The teenage batting sensation was part of the Indian men’s cricket team that defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in the final to win gold.Sooryavanshi made an aggressive start, hitting two consecutive sixes, before Saim Ayub dismissed him for 15 off nine balls. Despite his early exit, India went on to win the final and secure a memorable gold medal.Mairaj makes history at 50Two-time Olympian Mairaj Ahmad Khan became India’s oldest medallist at the 2026 Asian Games at the age of 50. He won bronze as part of the men’s skeet shooting team alongside Anantjeet Singh Naruka and Bhavtegh Singh Gill.Khan has competed internationally for more than 20 years and is a three-time ISSF World Cup gold medallist. However, the bronze in Aichi-Nagoya was his first Asian Games medal.Overall, Japan’s 11-year-old eSports player Yuki Kurihara became the youngest gold medallist in Asian Games history after winning the Puyo Puyo Champions title. articles.title: España abre la defensa del título mundial con una goleada ante Francia
articles.standfirst: La selección femenina se impuso por 8-0 ante el conjunto galo en la competición que se disputa en Asunción
articles.summary: La selección femenina se impuso por 8-0 ante el conjunto galo en la competición que se disputa en Asunción
articles.body: La selección española femenina de hockey patines, vigente campeona mundial, comenzó este domingo en Asunción (Paraguay) la defensa del título con una contundente goleada ante Francia (8-0), en un estreno plácido que le permitió coger sensaciones antes de afrontar los compromisos más exigentes del torneo. El combinado dirigido por Sergi Macià cumplió los pronósticos en un partido que, sobre el papel, se presentaba propicio para iniciar el campeonato con confianza. Pese a las irregulares condiciones de la pista, que en algunos momentos dificultaron la estabilidad de las jugadoras, España impuso desde el inicio su superioridad y encarriló un triunfo sin apenas sobresaltos. Victòria Porta, con un triplete, lideró la producción ofensiva de la selección española, que también contó con los goles de María Sanjurjo, autora de un doblete, y de Aina Florenza, Sara Roces y Mariona Colomer. Francia, claramente inferior a la actual campeona, apenas pudo ofrecer resistencia ante una España que controló el encuentro de principio a fin y que aspira a revalidar el título conquistado en 2024 en Novara (Italia). El estreno no pudo ser mejor para el conjunto español, que este lunes afrontará un duelo previsiblemente más exigente ante Chile, también a las 22:45 hora española. En la tercera jornada llegará el gran duelo del Grupo A contra Argentina, segunda selección más laureada de la historia con seis títulos mundiales, un enfrentamiento que, salvo sorpresa, estará llamado a decidir el liderato del grupo. 8 - España: Ferrer; Florenza (1), Piquero, Sanjurjo (2), Porta (3), -cinco inicial-, Roces (1), Colomer (1), Blackman, Salvanyà y Salvat (p.s). 0 - Francia: Buchoux, Lagroye, Herrault, Célia Gohet, D'Haese, -cinco inicial-, Dubocquet, Solène, Gefflot, Husson y Lucie Gohet (p.s). Goles: 1-0, min.8: Florenza. 2-0, min.10: Sanjurjo. 3-0, min.22: Porta. 4-0, min.25: Sanjurjo. 5-0, min.34: Porta. 6-0, min.35: Roces. 7-0, min.45: Colomer. 8-0, min.48: Porta. Árbitros: Paulo Giraudo (ARG) y Leandro Tosoni (ARG). Sin amonestaciones. articles.title: Nuevo Hyundai Tucson: ¿cuáles son sus argumentos para convertirse en un súper ventas?
articles.standfirst: Hyundai ha renovado su popular Tucson, que ahora es más grande y estrena motores. Pero ahí no quedan sus novedades
articles.summary: Hyundai ha renovado su popular Tucson, que ahora es más grande y estrena motores con hasta 292 CV y 81 kilómetros de autonomía eléctrica
articles.body: Al Hyundai Tucson le ha ido muy bien desde que llegó al mercado la primera generación en 2004, con más de 2 millones de unidades vendidas en nuestro continente y el mérito de ser el SUV del segmento C más vendido en Europa en 2025. Pero el tiempo pasa y ya está lista la nueva generación, que como es de rigor en estos tiempos gana espacio por dentro y da un salto importante en tecnología y electrificación. Aún habrá que esperar para comprobar cómo se plasma su sentido práctico en el día a día, pero empecemos conformándonos con la información que ya hemos podido conocer. El nuevo Tucson mide 4,56 metros de largo, 1,90 de ancho y 1,67 de alto. Son 3,5 centímetros más de longitud y anchura y 2 centímetros más de altura que el modelo anterior, mientras que la batalla crece 4 centímetros, hasta 2,72 metros, para ofrecer esa mayor amplitud prometida, que se acompaña de un maletero que anuncia hasta 695 litros. El diseño también cambia por completo, y dado que resulta bastante atractivo puede que aquí tenga uno de sus mayores atributos para seguir siendo un súper ventas. La filosofía Art of Steel, se reconoce sobre todo en unos pasos de rueda muy marcados, una carrocería de aspecto más musculoso y una nueva firma luminosa que delante lleva la iluminación H-Edge y detrás unas luces con efecto tridimensional. En determinadas versiones habrá además iluminación Micro Pixel con 25.600 LED individuales. Pero es muy posible que sea dentro donde el cambio resulte más interesante para quien vaya a utilizar un Tucson a diario. Hyundai ha optado por un salpicadero de dos niveles, con una pantalla digital de 9,9 pulgadas para el conductor y una pantalla central que puede alcanzar las 17 pulgadas. Y hay un detalle que parece pequeño pero que dice bastante de por dónde van las tendencias: vuelven (por fin) los botones físicos para las funciones que más empleamos. Es decir, que no todo tenga que pasar por un menú táctil. Una de las principales novedades de este sistema multimedia (se llama Pleos Connect) es Gleo, un asistente de voz apoyado en inteligencia artificial que, aseguran, entiende órdenes en lenguaje natural y puede acceder a información en tiempo real. También habrá actualizaciones de software a distancia, llave digital para teléfonos y relojes compatibles y, como opción, un equipo de sonido Bang & Olufsen de 12 altavoces. Hay otras soluciones menos llamativas pero quizá más útiles en el día a día. El Tucson puede incorporar dos cargadores inalámbricos de 15W y cuatro tomas USB-C de hasta 100 W. Además, el cambio automático pasa a manejarse mediante un selector situado en la columna de dirección, por lo que libera espacio entre los asientos. Y los pasajeros traseros disponen de una segunda fila que puede desplazarse 15 centímetros y plegarse en proporción 40:20:40. Hyundai también estrena en el Tucson una función denominada HEV Stay. En determinadas paradas permite mantener funcionando el climatizador, el equipo de sonido y la carga de dispositivos con el motor de gasolina apagado. Es una de esas funciones que sobre el papel puede parecer secundaria, pero que evita eso que por desgracia hace tanta gente y que consiste en esperar a los niños en la puerta del colegio o a la pareja en la del supermercado con el motor encendido (y el coche contaminando) porque quieren seguir con el climatizador encendido. La gama mecánica mantiene el motor 1.6 T-GDI como punto de partida, con 150 CV y posibilidad de asociarlo a un cambio manual de seis velocidades o a una transmisión de doble embrague de siete marchas con sistema de hibridación ligera de 48 voltios. Por encima aparece el Tucson híbrido, con 245 CV y 380 Nm, mientras que el híbrido enchufable alcanza los 292 CV y anuncia hasta 81 kilómetros de autonomía eléctrica con llantas de 17 pulgadas. El Tucson HEV acelera de 0 a 100 km/h en 8,3 segundos con tracción delantera y en 7,9 segundos con tracción total. El PHEV mantiene los 380 Nm de par y utiliza una batería de 17,1 kWh que admite cargas en corriente alterna de hasta 7,2 kW. En cuanto a capacidad de remolque, el híbrido llega hasta 1.910 kg y el enchufable hasta 1.810 kg. La parte de seguridad también recibe una actualización importante. El nuevo Tucson incorpora siete airbags, incluido uno central delantero, una estructura con acero de alta resistencia y nuevos sistemas de asistencia. Entre ellos está un sistema de monitorización del conductor que utiliza cámaras para detectar la mirada (debería funcionar incluso si llevas gafas de sol) y posibles signos de somnolencia. También puede avisar de la presencia de ocupantes en las plazas traseras y de la posible presencia de niños dentro del vehículo. Hay incluso tecnología pensada para situaciones muy concretas. El Memory Reverse Assist puede registrar hasta 50 metros de recorrido y reproducir después esa trayectoria marcha atrás controlando la dirección. Los modelos con tracción 4x4 pueden incorporar una cámara que permite visualizar la zona situada alrededor y debajo del coche, mientras que el sistema de aparcamiento remoto puede mover el vehículo para entrar o salir de una plaza sin que el conductor esté dentro. El nuevo Tucson se fabricará para Europa en la planta de Hyundai en la República Checa. De momento lo podremos contemplar por primera vez en vivo en el próximo Salón de París, y todavía no sabemos ni su fecha de aparición exacta en el mercado ni sus precios.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal amenaza el trono de Ronaldo Nazário
articles.standfirst: El extremo del Barcelona toma la delantera para convertirse en el Balón de Oro más joven de todos los tiempos
articles.summary: El extremo del Barcelona toma la delantera para convertirse en el Balón de Oro más joven de todos los tiempos
articles.body: Lamine Yamal lleva pulverizando récords de precocidad desde que debutase a nivel profesional con apenas 15 años. Por el camino, el extremo del Barcelona ha ido desbancando a algunos de los mejores jugadores de la historia y ahora tiene un nuevo reto por delante: arrebatarle a Ronaldo Nazário el prestigio de ser el Balón de Oro más joven de todos los tiempos. El brasileño conquistó el galardón en 1997, después de brillar en su primera temporada en el Barcelona y fichar por el Inter de Milán, cuando tenía 21 años, tres meses y cinco días. Desde entonces, nadie ha conseguido superar esa marca. Ni siquiera Lionel Messi o Cristiano Ronaldo, dos de los grandes dominadores en la historia del galardón individual más prestigioso del fútbol. Lamine Yamal, sin embargo, está en disposición de hacerlo con un margen considerable, puesto que acaba de cumplir 19 años hace apenas unos meses. Las votaciones ya están cerradas desde hace una semana, pero su cotización no ha dejado de crecer en las apuestas deportivas. Bwin ya le sitúa como máximo favorito para conquistar el Balón de Oro con una cuota de 1.46, por delante de Harry Kane (2.50) y Kylian Mbappé (15.0). Lamine, mientras tanto, continúa centrado en lo que ocurre dentro del terreno de juego. Ha comenzado la temporada 'volando' con el Barcelona y también está trasladando ese estado de forma a la Selección. Su impacto con España está siendo mayúsculo y sus actuaciones en la Nations League están confirmando que no se trata únicamente de una racha puntual. El joven azulgrana ya ha convertido la búsqueda de récords en algo habitual... aunque el próximo podría colocarle directamente en una página reservada hasta ahora para Ronaldo Nazário. Las mejores casas de apuestas siguen muy pendientes de su evolución y Bwin también le concede un claro favoritismo en el siguiente reto que tiene por delante con España. Después de marcar ante Inglaterra, Croacia y Chequia, Lamine ha conseguido, por primera vez en su carrera, enlazar tres partidos consecutivos viendo portería con la Selección. Ahora, buscará cerrar el parón internacional de la mejor manera posible y prolongar una racha que le ha convertido en uno de los grandes protagonistas de esta Fecha FIFA. Ante Croacia, en Split, tendrá la oportunidad de volver a marcar y seguir alimentando una temporada que espera que acabe siendo histórica. Bwin paga a 1.93 que Lamine Yamal vea puerta y vuelva a demostrar que su techo todavía está muy lejos de alcanzarse. El Balón de Oro sería el siguiente gran récord en caer y, si finalmente lo consigue, desbancará a Ronaldo Nazário como el ganador más joven de la historia.

articles.title: Formula One to probe software bug behind Bahrain GP chaos in Sepang
articles.summary: Drivers faced glitches at the race in Malaysia, where Lewis Hamilton had to stop and restart his car on the track.
articles.body:
Formula One’s governing body has promised a full investigation into a software bug that caused chaos and forced the start of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to be aborted, with drivers feeling like they were in battery-powered cars made of Lego.

Ferrari’s seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull’s four-time champion and eventual race winner Max Verstappen were among several affected by the glitch on a formation lap after torrential rain and a long delay at Malaysia’s steamy Sepang circuit on Sunday.

Verstappen compared the experience to a “Lego race” held at Silverstone before the British Grand Prix while Hamilton, the sport’s most successful driver of all time, had to stop his car on track and restart it in what he said was a career first.

The episode was the latest in a difficult first season for the new era of cars and engines, with drivers at the pinnacle of motorsport unhappy since the opening race with the power units’ increased electrical component and the need for energy management.

FIA said afterwards that “an unprecedented combination of low engine speed, low-grip conditions, wet-weather energy management settings and the Sepang circuit’s sector configuration led to an unintended loss of power for a number of cars”.

“As a result, the FIA technical department removed the energy limit constraint in the affected sectors through an updated software release distributed to all competitors during the race delay caused by heavy rain, enabling teams to make the necessary changes to the power unit before the start of the race.

“This issue had not been detected by the FIA or the teams during testing or during the laps to the grid. The FIA, together with the teams and power unit manufacturers, will undertake a full review of the issue.”

The FIA’s single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis told reporters the lack of preseason testing in wet conditions had played a part in the chaos.

“Some cars went very slowly, almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars, and some cars almost stopped completely,” he said. “That bug prevented the power from being redeployed, and for the cars to start again.

“I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time, and not have such a situation.”

Sepang was the first race weekend of the season with wet conditions, although the track dried during the race.

“Sometimes things fall through the net and people learn, and you do a better job next time,” Tombazis said.

articles.summary: Loreto Peinado se hizo con la victoria en la especialidad el sábado, mientras que su hermano Guillermo hizo lo propio el domingo
articles.body: Hablar de los hermanos Peinado es hablar de escalada... y de campeones de España de la modalidad de bloque. No es habitual que dos miembros de una familia se encaramen a lo más alto del podio nacional... en el mismo fin de semana. Pero eso fue lo que ocurrió en Cáceres, donde se disputó el Supercampeonato de España en el rocódromo Alberto Ginés. Aunque no se encontraba a priori entre las favoritas al título, Loreto Peinado se proclamó campeona de España de bloque, tras encadenar dos de los cuatro bloques de la final: sumó 69,1 puntos. Geila Macià y Paula Traverso completaron el podio femenino absoluto. Apenas 24 horas después, su hermano Guillermo hizo lo propio en la prueba masculina de esta modalidad. El madrileño fue el único finalista que pudo encadenar un bloque, el cuarto, y sumó zona en los otros tres para terminar con 54,9 puntos. Manuel Pastor fue plata (29,4 puntos) y Hugo Martín, bronce. "Estoy muy contento", aseguró Guillermo Peinado en declaraciones a la Federación. "Eran bloques bastantes duros. Me encuentro muy bien y fuerte, he estado viajando últimamente mucho a Francia, a Japón...para prepararme".

articles.title: Nike CEO may have just admitted the company went too woke as stock hits 12-year low
articles.summary: Nike CEO Elliott Hill's memo acknowledged the need to refocus on sport after years of political campaigns featuring Colin Kaepernick and others.
articles.body: The Nike CEO's memo to his employees was 860 words. But here were the 33 that stuck out: "Over the past year, we've put sport at the center of everything we do. We're seeing encouraging signs of progress, but we have more work to do to win over the long term." That was sent out on Oct. 1, one day before Nike's stock price closed at $33.87 per share — its lowest in over 12 years. The once unstoppable athletic titan expects more layoffs in 2027 after already cutting staff twice this year. TED CRUZ TAKES VICTORY LAP AS ICONIC AMERICAN BRAND'S STOCK PLUNGES TO 12-YEAR LOW And you have to wonder if those words above — "over the past year, we've put sport at the center of everything we do" — was as much a confession as it was a mission statement. Nike chose politics over its core identity, and it's desperately trying to course correct. Last month, Outkick's Dan Zaksheske listed a series of decisions the company made over the past few years aimed at courting a left-wing audience. In 2019, it tapped Colin Kaepernick as the face of its 30th anniversary "Just Do It" campaign. In the wake of George Floyd's death in 2020, it ran its "For Once, Don't Do it" ad, which included lines like "don't pretend there's not a problem in America," and "Don't turn your back on racism." In 2023, it partnered with female-identifying male Dylan Mulvaney to promote women's leggings and sports bras — seemingly unfazed by the backlash Mulvaney's partnership with Bud Light sparked. There was also the "Equality" commercial in 2017 that featured phrases such as "the ball should bounce the same for everyone." NIKE SHAREHOLDERS REJECT TRANSPARENCY PROPOSAL AS FAITH-BASED FIRM QUESTIONS DEI COMMITMENTS Now, it wouldn't be fair to say that any one of these campaigns sunk the swoosh's stock on their own. Nike's stock hit an all-time closing high of $177.51 per share in November 2021. But the fact that it has dipped 81% since then? It's hard not to tie a big chunk of that to the brand's regular offerings at the wokeness altar. One of its more glaring gaffes within the past couple years is the delay of Caitlin Clark's signature sneaker. As sports writers such as Ethan Strauss and Dan Wetzel have pointed out, Nike didn't drop Clark's shoe until June of this year. Strauss wrote earlier that the company felt like it had to debut A'ja Wilson's sneaker before Clark's despite Wilson ranking fifth in WNBA jersey sales and Clark ranking first. Although A'ja is almost certainly the best player in the WNBA, nothing moves women's basketball fans (or hoop fans in general?) like anything associated with Caitlin. CAITLIN CLARK UNVEILS NIKE CAITLIN 1 AS HER FIRST SIGNATURE SHOE WITH AN OCTOBER RELEASE DATE THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! This wasn't necessarily a case of Nike putting sports on the back burner. But it did reek of identity politics, which has a way of becoming expensive when a company loses sight of what its customers actually want. Nike seems to have realized this, but it took it being knocked out of the S&P 100 for the brass to actually do something about it. Which brings us back to the aforementioned memo. Nike CEO Elliott Hill didn't use that note to dwell on the company's past campaigns and advertisements. He mentioned Nike establishing a new campus in India. He emphasized accelerating supply chain modernization efforts. He discussed Nike's plan to organize into three geographic regions — Americas (North America and Latin America), APGC (Asia Pacific and Greater China) and EMEA (Europe, the Middle East and Africa). But it's hard to overlook that one-sentence acknowledgment about prioritizing sport. The injection of politics into athletics is almost always a guarantee to shift eyeballs elsewhere. The cratering of NBA ratings post 2020 certainly reinforced that notion. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Seems the injection of politics into athletic brands can be just as corrosive. Nike went woke a while ago, and it may finally be waking up to the damage that was caused. OutKick reached out to Nike for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

articles.title: After Asian Games disappointment, PV Sindhu and Indian shuttlers eye fresh start at Arctic Open
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian badminton will look to turn the page on a disappointing Asian Games campaign when the BWF World Tour resumes with the USD 500,000 Arctic
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian badminton will look to turn the page on a disappointing Asian Games campaign when the BWF World Tour resumes with the USD 500,000 Arctic Open Super 500 in Finland on Tuesday, with two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu leading the country's challenge.India's shuttlers returned from the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games with just one medal and four quarterfinal finishes, two medals fewer than their tally at the previous edition in Hangzhou. Badminton was among the major disappointments, having contributed three medals at Hangzhou, including a gold.India eventually finished fourth in the overall Asian Games standings with 85 medals, including 21 gold, but the badminton campaign left plenty of room for improvement.Sindhu looks to build on Japan Open triumphSindhu, who lost a tight women's singles quarterfinal to China's Chen Yufei at the Asian Games, will be looking for a strong response in Finland.The 31-year-old former world champion has, however, enjoyed some encouraging results this season. She won the Japan Open and also reached the quarterfinals of the World Championships in New Delhi.Sindhu has been handed a qualifier in the opening round and will hope to make the most of a favourable start as she looks to regain consistency on the World Tour.In men's singles, former world No. 1 Kidambi Srikanth and HS Prannoy will also be eager to rediscover their best form. Both were part of India's bronze-medal-winning men's team at the Asian Games but did not feature in a match.Srikanth, who reached the final of the US Open Super 300 earlier this year, will begin against Canada's Brian Yang.Prannoy faces a significantly tougher opening assignment against fourth seed Anders Antonsen of Denmark. The 34-year-old Kerala shuttler has struggled for consistency since last year, although he did reach the quarterfinals of the Vietnam Open recently.Youngsters bring fresh momentumIndia's women's singles challenge also features several players who have enjoyed encouraging results this season.Tanvi Sharma, winner of the Taipei Open Super 300, will face Chinese Taipei's Chiu Pin-Chian, while Vietnam Open Super 100 runner-up Isharani Baruah has drawn top seed Ratchanok Intanon of Thailand.Ashmita Chaliha, who claimed her maiden BWF World Tour title at the Korea Masters Super 300, will open against seventh seed Line Christophersen of Denmark.Unnati Hooda will face China's Han Qian Xi after making headlines at the Asian Games by stunning world No. 6 Putri Kusuma Wardani of Indonesia.In men's doubles, Hariharan Amsakarunan and MR Arjun take on England's Alex Green and Zach Russ. articles.title: 3-Way Trade Ideas for Connor Hellebuyck and Alexander Nikishin Amid NHL Rumors
articles.summary: Connor Hellebuyck is still technically a member of the Winnipeg Jets, even if his time with the team seems over.
articles.body:
Connor Hellebuyck is still technically a member of the Winnipeg Jets, even if his time with the team seems over.

He wants a trade, did not report to training camp, and is currently suspended while the team tries to find a deal that brings back enough value to salvage the situation.

One team that reportedly has a serious interest in him is the Carolina Hurricanes. While they have mostly competed without a top-tier goalie, including the 2025-26 Stanley Cup-winning team, that doesn't mean they would turn down the chance to get one if it were to arise.

The opportunity might be presenting itself, especially given their remaining salary-cap space and the potential trade assets they have at their disposal.

The most logical trade asset is defenseman Alexander Nikishin, who remains unsigned as a restricted free agent.

The problem: Winnipeg may not be very interested in Nikishin because there may be concerns about his willingness to sign there. The Russian defenseman is believed to want in the range of $9 million per year on a long-term deal.

Sportsnet NHL Insider Elliotte Friedman recently suggested Carolina could be looking to use Nikishin as part of a three-team trade to help Winnipeg get what it is looking for, while also getting Hellebuyck to Carolina. Hellebuyck has a cap hit of $8.5 million , and the Canes currently have over $10 million in cap space, according to Puckpedia.

The other wrinkle? Hellebuyck's no-move clause has made it difficult for the Jets to find the right trading partner. A three-way deal is complicated as it is, and adding Hellebuyck's no-move clause into the mix makes it doubly tough.

Nevertheless, let's try to come up with some three-team ideas that could make sense for all involved.

St. Louis receives: D Alexander Nikishin, G Pyotr Kochetkov

Winnipeg receives: G Joel Hofer, F prospect Felix Unger Sorum, first-round pick (from Carolina), first-round pick (from St. Louis).

Even after picking up Clay Stevenson off waivers before the season and with veteran Stuart Skinner on a two-year deal, the Jets will probably want a goalie in any trade involving Hellebuyck.

Stevenson is an intriguing player, but he is largely unproven at age 27, and there is no way they are going to commit to him being any sort of a long-term answer at this point.

Blues goalie Jordan Binnington has no-trade protections in his contract and could block a deal to Winnipeg, yet the Blues still seem to value him as their starter despite his inconsistent play. All of that would work out in the Jets' favor because Hofer is probably the better goalie.

The Blues would come away with a young defenseman in Nikishin who would upgrade their blue line and fit the core they are building around Robert Thomas, Dylan Holloway, Jimmy Snuggerud, Jake Neighbours and Philip Broberg. While those players are at different stages of their development, Nikishin would align with St. Louis' effort to build a young, talented group capable of competing together over the long term.

The price from St. Louis would be Hofer and a first-round pick, which is probably close to fair value. Simon Nemec—a similarly skilled player at a comparable point in his career, with similar production—was traded for two first-round picks earlier this summer. In this scenario, Hofer effectively replaces the second first-rounder.

Carolina would part with Nikishin, Kochetkov, Unger Sorum, and one of its four first-round picks over the next three years, which is probably a similar type of value it would give up if it were just directly dealing with Winnipeg, and if Winnipeg wanted Nikishin.

The question would be whether this is enough for Winnipeg. Hofer is a solid goalie, but he's not Hellebuyck. He's younger, but he's also a restricted free agent after this season, and there's always the question of whether he would sign there.

Two first-round picks would represent meaningful value, though their ultimate worth would depend heavily on where they land.

Pittsburgh receives: D Alexander Nikishin

Winnipeg receives: G prospect Joel Blomqvist, F Tommy Novak, F prospect Charlie Cerrato, first-round pick (from Carolina)

Pittsburgh Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas has been extremely active and aggressive over the past couple of years, and he has made no secret of being in the market for any young, talented player who is available.

Nikishin checks a lot of the boxes and could fill a significant long-term need on defense.

Erik Karlsson and Sam Girard are both unrestricted free agents after this season. Kris Letang is getting into his late 30s. They have a really good defensive prospect in Harrison Brunicke, but they could use another long-term piece.

The Penguins also have the salary cap space to sign Nikishin. They have forward depth at the NHL level to deal, and they have goalie depth in their farm system. This proposal has Pittsburgh dealing from positions of strength to address a long-term weakness on defense.

From a Winnipeg perspective, we are going to switch things up a little and go with the idea that they do not necessarily need an NHL goalie back right away, and instead try to rebuild some forward depth.

Novak is by no means a star, but he is a solid, middle-six center who is signed for the long term on a very team-friendly contract.

Cerrato, a center prospect in the Carolina farm system, brings a tenacious style of play while still showing offensive upside that could give him a chance to become a long-term NHL player.

I am just going to call this the Tylenol trade because it is an attempt to solve everybody's headaches.

Or in the case of the Red Wings, at least one of their headaches is because who really even knows what is going on with center Dylan Larkin.

Carolina cannot get Nikishin signed and wants to use him as a trade piece for Hellebuyck, but Winnipeg does not want him.

Detroit cannot get Edvinsson signed, and now he reportedly prefers a trade away from the Red Wings .

Well, let's just get rid of everybody in exchange for everybody else. Nikishin from Carolina to Detroit for Edvinsson; Edvinsson from Carolina to Winnipeg for Hellebuyck.

Is it perfect? No. Probably not. But somebody has to get something done here.

articles.title: New WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Match Card Predictions
articles.summary: With each passing week, the lineup for WWE Money in the Bank 2026 has become more and more appealing.
articles.body:
With each passing week, the lineup for WWE Money in the Bank 2026 has become more and more appealing.

Less than a week out from the event, the card is not yet complete with Stephanie Vaquer's Women's World Championship challenger needing to be determined, but everything else that's set in stone has the potential to be special.

The fields for the men's and women's Money in the Bank ladder matches have been filled out as of Friday's SmackDown and largely consist of fresh faces.

Meanwhile, Oba Femi and Bronson Reed should have a hard-hitting affair when they wage war, and Roman Reigns' World Heavyweight Championship defense against LA Knight has been built up exceptionally well.

Every matchup feels genuinely unpredictable, which is in line with how exciting past installments of the event have been. Contracts have been cashed in the same night, championships have changed hands in shocking fashion and Superstars have returned after lengthy absences, so there's no telling what this year's show will have in store.

These are the latest predictions for Money in the Bank on Saturday.

Participants: Roxanne Perez, Sol Ruca, Lola Vice, Jacy Jayne, Lash Legend, Tiffany Stratton

Tiffany Stratton is the only competitor involved in this year's women's Money in the Bank ladder match to have previously held either the WWE Women's or Women's World Championship, as every other participant debuted on the main roster within the last year and a half.

Stratton has had a budding friendship with reigning WWE women's champ Chelsea Green in recent months, so it is possible she could win the ladder match for a second time in her career and cash in on Green. However, she can still turn heel on Green and take the title from her without winning Money in the Bank.

Lola Vice recently arrived on Raw, so it's too early for her to be holding the briefcase. Lash Legend and Sol Ruca can have solid showings in the bout but aren't in a spot currently where they're ready to win a world title, either.

That leaves Roxanne Perez and Jacy Jayne as the best possible options, and of the two, there's a stronger story to tell with Perez, especially since Jayne already has the Women's United States Championship in her possession.

Perez becoming Ms. Money in the Bank would undoubtedly cause friction within The Judgment Day and most likely lead her to winning the women's world title that Liv Morgan will want back.

Oba Femi and Bronson Reed have been on a collision course since Reed returned at Sunday Night's Main Event a month ago and immediately targeted Femi.

The Ruler then shifted his sights from Bron Breakker to Reed, focusing less on the future and more on the right here and now.

Reed has been made to feel like a legitimate threat to Femi and justifiably so. He has come back in the best shape of his entire career, has sounded sharp on the mic and has gotten the better of The Ruler on more than one occasion.

That's why it would be a mistake for Femi to straight-up beat Reed at Money in the Bank before moving on to what's next.

If Femi isn't challenging for a world championship until WrestleMania 43 at the earliest, he needs formidable foes to keep him busy and Reed is the perfect opponent for him.

Femi vs. Breakker already ended in a disqualification, so it would be lazy to do something similar on this show, so Reed winning would be the better outcome.

Even if it's in fluky fashion, Reed besting the man who retired Brock Lesnar would be a massive boost for him, and Femi would hardly be hindered by the loss.

Perhaps the rest of The Vision factor into the finish in some form or fashion, but either way, Reed winning is a must.

Women's World Championship: Stephanie Vaquer vs. Liv Morgan or Becky Lynch

The returns of Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch on Raw in the wake of SummerSlam injected some much-needed excitement into the Women's World Championship picture.

Vaquer went on to dethrone Liv Morgan for the title in her native Chile in mid-September and made it clear that she intends to welcome all comers to her coveted title.

It's been announced that Morgan and Lynch will fight for the next shot at the strap on Monday's Raw, with the winner getting their opportunity at Money in the Bank this weekend. It still feels too soon to be doing the first-ever one-on-one outing between Vaquer and Lynch, and Vaquer vs. Morgan has already happened three times since WrestleMania 42.

The most interesting scenario would see Vaquer defending the belt against both former champs in a Triple Threat at the event. That would require Morgan vs. Lynch ending in some sort of non-finish or a draw on Raw, but it's the only logical endgame for the feud at this point.

As noted, Vaquer is less than a month into her run with the prestigious prize and shouldn't be dropping it anytime soon, or at least until she gets to battle Lynch in a singles setting. Regardless of what her title match at Money in the Bank looks like, Vaquer should retain.

World Heavyweight Championship: Roman Reigns vs. LA Knight

LA Knight's steady rise back to the top of the card on Raw has been encouraging to see. The rekindling of his rivalry with Roman Reigns has also had its fair share of memorable moments and has made for fun television since SummerSlam.

However, nothing of what Knight accomplished prior to this point matters if he can't win "the big one." He has found himself on the cusp of breaking through the proverbial glass ceiling and becoming world champion on plenty of past occasions, but it has seemed that WWE brass simply don't see him as being on that level.

It's now or never for Knight, and all signs point to him falling short when it matters most yet again.

Reigns vs. Oba Femi is surely penciled in for the main event of WrestleMania 43 and WWE presumably will not want Reigns dropping the belt before then. Knight could absolutely hold the gold briefly after beating Reigns with an assist from Solo Sikoa or The 946, but there's been nothing to suggest they're actually headed in that direction.

Knight will fight valiantly as he always does and prove he belongs, only to eat defeat and be demoted back to the midcard scene that he's outgrown.

Participants: Bron Breakker, Je'Von Evans, Penta, Trick Williams, CM Punk, Kevin Owens

Much like the women's match, the men's installment features an abundance of new blood as well as a number of plausible outcomes.

Je'Von Evans is the least likely winner but should still shine with his aerial excellence. Trick Williams is another future world champion but is in the midst of his second run as United States champion and shouldn't be headlining major events for top titles just yet.

CM Punk has captured the briefcase twice before in his career and can easily challenge for a world championship at any time, so giving it to him again would be a waste. Although Kevin Owens is a former world champ as well, it's been almost a decade since his last reign, and being Mr. Money in the Bank would make for a fun story while Sami Zayn is the undisputed WWE champion.

Bron Breakker and Penta are the strongest candidates of everyone involved, but the latter advancing after not originally being scheduled for a qualifier gives him the slight edge. His career-altering performance with Roman Reigns put him on a path for superstardom, and clinching the contract would virtually guarantee him an eventual run with a world title.

Breakker can and will be in a top spot someday, but Penta has much more to gain from going over in this one.

articles.title: AJ Styles Teases Return, Matt Cardona Explains Pay Cut & WWE Rumors on WrestleMania 43 in Las Vegas
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

WWE Hall of Famer AJ Styles laid his gloves down in the ring and ended his career earlier this year, but it sounds like there's a chance he could lace up his wrestling boots once again.

During an appearance on What Do You Wanna Talk About? with Cody Rhodes, Styles was asked if he reserves the right to end his retirement if he ever wants to, and The Phenomenal One affirmed that he could make a comeback if he ever gets the itch to return to the ring.

"Yep. I mean, it's retirement. I think Michael Jordan said it once. It means if I want to come back, I come back," Styles told Rhodes (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News).

Styles made it clear that he's not announcing a return, but when Rhodes followed up by asking if Styles considers his career to be completely "over, over," the 49-year-old said, "I don't think I can. No."

Styles ended his career with a loss against Gunther at the 2026 Royal Rumble premium live event in his hometown of Atlanta in January. He said he was content with how his retirement played out.

"I was hoping that I would get to lay him down in Atlanta. Yeah. That's what I wanted to do," Styles said. "The Dirty South. But there's all kinds of things running through my mind, but I am certainly glad I got the opportunity to lay them down in Atlanta. That was a great moment for me and my family to be able to do that, and I felt good about it. I felt at peace with it, and so I'm glad it happened there."

Styles is one of the greatest wrestlers of his generation, so fans would surely welcome the chance to see him perform in the ring again.

Matt Cardona Reveals Why He Took Pay Cut to Rejoin WWE

Before returning to WWE in January, Matt Cardona was one of the biggest stars on the independent circuit, but he couldn't turn down the opportunity to chase his dream.

While speaking with Jeremy Jacobowitz, Cardona revealed that he accepted less money to return to WWE because of the opportunities that come with being part of the biggest wrestling company in the world.

"I made more money outside WWE than I ever made in WWE. Like, I technically took a pay cut to go back to WWE. You know what I'm saying? That's how much money I was making on the indies," Cardona said (h/t Derek Holloway of Ringside News). "But WWE, going back, is the ultimate opportunity. 'Cause if it works out, it'll be the ultimate raise, right? Like, I'm sitting here talking to you because WWE set this up."

Cardona called his initial release from WWE "the greatest day of my life" because it allowed him to develop a new version of himself as he rebuilt his Superstar resume.

"I wanted to create something new, and that's why I decided, 'Okay, I'm going to reinvent myself, and I'm going to change the Matt Cardona game. Yeah, hopefully WWE wants me back, but if they don't, that's fine,'" he said.

Cardona is currently recovering from a triceps injury, but it's clear that he's where he wants to be as he tries to work his way to the main-event scene in WWE.

While the last two WrestleManias have been held in Las Vegas, WWE's biggest show won't be heading to Sin City for a third year in a row.

WrestleMania 43 is scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia, but many have wondered whether Las Vegas would serve as a backup location if there were any travel concerns.

However, Dave Meltzer stated in the latest Wrestling Observer Newsletter that Las Vegas is off the table in April 2027.

"Regarding rumors of Las Vegas as a backup plan, sources in Las Vegas who have basically tipped us off on all the Mania decisions as well as issues with the dates that had to be taken care of the past two years well ahead of time, said that the city does not have the dates available in April and is not able to spend the kind of money they have in the past to bring the event in," Meltzer stated (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News).

WWE has yet to confirm the date for WrestleMania 43, so plans could change if any potential issues arise. Per Carrier, Meltzer stated that "contingency plans would still be necessary given the uncertainty surrounding travel conditions, but the company intends to move forward unless the situation becomes too dangerous."

While Las Vegas provided a beautiful backdrop for WrestleMania 41 and 42, it's safe to say that WrestleMania 43 will have a different energy whether it's held in Saudi Arabia or somewhere else.

articles.title: Cadillac driver Valtteri Bottas takes on 350km cycling challenge from Malaysia to Singapore for next race after F1 setback
articles.summary: Valtteri Bottas has taken on an unusual challenge after a difficult Malaysian Grand Prix.
articles.body: Valtteri Bottas has taken on an unusual challenge after a difficult Malaysian Grand Prix. The Cadillac driver has decided to cycle around 350km from Kuala Lumpur International Airport to Singapore ahead of the next Formula 1 race. The Finnish driver began his journey after the race and covered 56.6km on his opening day.Bottas is an experienced cyclist and regularly takes part in demanding gravel events. His latest ride will take him across Malaysia as he prepares for the Singapore Grand Prix on October 11. The journey comes after his disappointing race at Sepang, where he crashed early after taking a gamble on slick tyres during wet conditions.Valtteri Bottas begins 350km ride ahead of Singapore Grand PrixWhile most F1 drivers will travel to Singapore by plane, Valtteri Bottas has chosen a very different route.The 37-year-old plans to cycle from Kuala Lumpur International Airport to Singapore. The total journey is expected to cover around 350km.Bottas has already started the challenge. During his first day, he rode 56.6km from Kuala Lumpur International Airport towards Port Dickson.Long-distance cycling also gives Bottas a way to train away from the F1 circuit. The physical demands can help his endurance. The mental challenge can also help him prepare for the intense demands of a Grand Prix weekend.His decision comes at an important point in his 2026 season.Bottas returned to a full-time F1 seat this year after spending the 2025 campaign as a reserve driver. He joined the new Cadillac Formula 1 Team alongside Mexican driver Sergio Perez.However, his comeback has been difficult so far.Bottas has yet to score a point this season. His best result remains 13th at the Chinese Grand Prix. He currently sits 22nd in the World Drivers’ Championship standings.His Malaysian Grand Prix ended in another disappointment.The Sepang race was moved onto the 2026 calendar after Formula 1 returned to Malaysia for the first time since 2017. The event was held as a replacement due to the ongoing situation in Iran.Bottas made a strategic gamble during the race by switching to slick tyres while the track remained wet. The decision did not work out. He crashed during the early stages and was forced to retire.The Singapore Grand Prix now presents another challenge.The Marina Bay Street Circuit is known for its demanding street layout, high temperatures and night-race conditions. Drivers also face a long and physically demanding race.Bottas has previous success at the venue. He finished third at the 2017 Singapore Grand Prix while driving for Mercedes. articles.title: From ending South Korea’s reign to booking 2028 LA Olympics quotas: Indian archers return from Asian Games with bigger target
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's archers returned home from the Asian Games with more than a record medal haul to celebrate.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's archers returned home from the Asian Games with more than a record medal haul to celebrate. They came back with history rewritten, Olympic qualification secured and the belief that the gap with the world's best is narrowing rapidly.The Indian contingent collected five gold, two silver and two bronze medals in Aichi-Nagoya, with both the compound and recurve squads producing landmark performances. The compound mixed team of Sahil Jadhav and Chikitha Taniparthu secured an Olympic quota place, while the recurve women's team ended South Korea's long-standing dominance by beating the 10-time Olympic champions 5-3 in the final.For a group that had faced questions before the Games, the response was emphatic. India's compound coach Dave Cousins believes the performance should put those doubts to rest.‘We proved exactly what they’re made of’Cousins said the coaching group had deliberately avoided making medal predictions before the Games, instead focusing on preparation and execution.“So early on, they wanted us to make predictions on how many medals we could get. The only thing we were willing to commit to is that our athletes would go prepared and that they would execute the process as best they could,” Cousins said.The results, he argued, were a reflection of a stronger support system around the archers.“When the training is right, the preparation is right and the ecosystem is right, these are the results you get. So we're very happy with that. We're exceptionally happy to clinch the first ever compound archery spot for the Olympic Games. That's a huge thing for us right now,” he added.The success was particularly significant because much of the compound squad was relatively inexperienced on the biggest international stage.“You in the media and the global archery community really had a lot of questions about our younger archers, the new squad. Well, I think we proved exactly what they're made of,” Cousins said.Jadhav and Taniparthu were at the heart of that response. Their mixed-team gold not only delivered another Asian Games title but also secured India's Olympic quota place.Jadhav said the final against Chinese Taipei was less about pressure and more about sticking to a plan repeatedly rehearsed in training.“It feels fantastic, and seeing this grand welcome gives us even more joy. There wasn't pressure as such because we had practised specifically for these situations,” Jadhav said. “It was all about execution, and we delivered. Now I feel all the hard work I've put in so far has truly paid off.”Taniparthu said the victory had given the young group another reason to work harder.“This feels so good and happy, and by this we will get motivated that we have to win more, do more hard work, then every time we will also get this,” she said.The compound women's team also underlined India's growing strength by equalling the world record score during its 238-234 victory over China. Taniparthu won that gold alongside veteran Jyothi Surekha Vennam and Prithika Pradeep.Sahil was also part of the men's gold-medal-winning team, while Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru won men's team gold and individual bronze. Kushal Dalal was another member of the men's gold-winning side.‘We thought that we would do it, and we did’The recurve contingent produced its own piece of history.Kumkum Mohod emerged as one of India's biggest individual stars, winning women's individual gold and helping the country secure women's team gold and mixed team silver. Her individual triumph also secured an Olympic quota for India.The 17-year-old said the result was the product of collective preparation rather than an individual effort.“What we thought would happen, happened. It was the team's hard work, all the team's motivation, and the support of the Archery Association of India and SAI. That's why everything happened,” she said.In the individual final against South Korea's Oh Yejin, Kumkum consciously shut out the opponent and concentrated on her own shooting.“In the final match, I completely enjoyed my shooting. I held on to my feeling, just shot my arrows and didn't look at who was ahead,” she said.Her advice after the breakthrough was equally simple.“Just stay disciplined and do your best at your work. Don't get carried away. Just keep doing your work properly,” she added.But it was the women's team victory over 10-time Olympic champions South Korea that arguably carried the biggest historical significance. Kirti Sharma was part of the side that defeated the Koreans 5-3, ending their dominance in the event.“India's first gold in this event. We beat Korea to win gold, so this created history for us. I feel very good that I was part of the team that created that history,” Sharma said.The magnitude of the challenge was not lost on the Indian team.“There was pressure because that team always took gold, so there was pressure on us, but we thought that we would do it, and we did,” Sharma said.Bigger target: LA 2028The men's recurve squad also contributed to India's medal haul, with Dhiraj Bommadevara winning silver in the mixed team event with Kumkum and another silver in the men's team event. Neeraj Chauhan claimed individual bronze and men's team silver, while Yashdeep Bhoge was part of the silver-winning men's team.Bommadevara believes the support structure around Indian archery has changed dramatically.“Earlier, there was hardly any support, and I relied closely on my family and friends. But if it weren't for this government, I wouldn't be standing here today. Our Prime Minister, our Sports Minister and our administrative setup have been so supportive,” he said.The pressure of an Asian Games, he added, was easier to manage because of the team's environment.“Pressure is there for everyone, but we were fortunate to have a team where we could stay cool and calm,” he said.And the next targets are already visible.“Next year, we have the World Championships, where Olympic quotas are there, and after that the LA Olympics,” he said.For Chauhan, the Asian Games was his first experience of the multi-sport event, and the medal made the occasion even more meaningful.“Overall, the experience of the Asian Games was very good. It was my first Asian Games. I went with the hope that I had to bring a medal for India, and bringing this medal has made me and my family very proud,” he said.Bhoge, making his debut, highlighted the collective spirit that helped India navigate the crucial moments.“Obviously it was my debut, so there were crunch moments, but everyone kept their morale up. The team stayed together. Because the whole team stayed together, we were able to play well and maintain ourselves,” he said.The Asian Games medals have therefore brought celebration, but also a bigger expectation. With Olympic quotas secured, South Korea's recurve dominance finally broken and a new generation of compound archers announcing themselves, India's archery programme now has a new benchmark.The Aichi-Nagoya triumph was historic. The next target is bigger — Los Angeles 2028.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kane says ‘Happy birthday to me!’ on X, but WWE fans mistake October 5 for his real birthday in a hilarious twist
articles.summary: WWE Hall of Famer Kane had fans scratching their heads on October 5 after posting a simple birthday message on X.
articles.body: WWE Hall of Famer Kane had fans scratching their heads on October 5 after posting a simple birthday message on X. The former WWE Champion wrote, “Happy birthday to me!”, sending many fans into the comments to wish him.October 5 marks the anniversary of Kane’s WWE debut. The masked star first appeared as Kane at Badd Blood: In Your House in 1997. Some fans quickly understood the reference, while others hilariously shared screenshots of Kane’s Wikipedia page showing his April 26 birthday.Kane’s WWE debut anniversary leaves fans confusedKane’s short X post on October 5 created an amusing situation among WWE fans.The former wrestler and Knox County mayor wrote, “Happy birthday to me!” without explaining what he meant. Fans immediately flooded the comments with birthday wishes.For some, the message appeared to be a normal birthday post. Kane was born Glenn Thomas Jacobs on April 26, 1967, in Spain. That means October 5 is not his actual birthday.However, October 5 holds huge importance in Kane’s professional wrestling career.It was on this date in 1997 that Kane made his famous WWE debut. He appeared at Badd Blood: In Your House and changed the course of The Undertaker’s storyline.Kane arrived during the first-ever Hell in a Cell match between The Undertaker and Shawn Michaels. The massive masked wrestler ripped the door off the Hell in a Cell structure before entering the ring.He then attacked The Undertaker with his brother’s own signature Tombstone Piledriver.The moment immediately established Kane as one of WWE’s most dangerous characters. He was presented as The Undertaker’s long-lost half-brother and a terrifying figure connected to fire.Kane went on to become one of the most recognisable stars in WWE history.His debut also began one of the company’s longest-running sibling rivalries. Kane and The Undertaker would fight each other several times before also becoming a hugely successful tag team known as the Brothers of Destruction.Still, not every fan understood Kane’s October 5 message immediately.Some followers genuinely wished him a happy birthday. Others eventually realised that he was celebrating the anniversary of his WWE debut.A few fans even posted screenshots from Kane’s Wikipedia page showing that his actual birthday is April 26.The confusion led to plenty of jokes in the comments.One fan wrote, “Make sure you blow out all four candles of the corner of the cake”, while adding a GIF of Kane’s signature fire entrance.The joke referred to Kane’s famous entrance, which featured flames shooting from the ring corners.Other fans used the occasion to celebrate the character’s impact. Many hailed Kane’s WWE debut as one of the greatest debuts in wrestling history.The timing also gave fans a chance to remember how quickly Kane became an important part of WWE. He later won the WWF Championship, World Heavyweight Championship and ECW Championship.He also became a WWE Grand Slam Champion and set several Royal Rumble records.Kane was eventually inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame as part of the Class of 2021.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: WWE Money in the Bank Winners Who Didn't Become the Stars Everyone Expected
articles.summary: Winning the Money in the Bank Ladder Match may be a fast-track to a main event push and a world title reign, but it does not guarantee success for every WWE Superstar who emerges from it victoriously.
articles.body:
Winning the Money in the Bank Ladder Match may be a fast-track to a main event push and a world title reign, but it does not guarantee success for every WWE Superstar who emerges from it victoriously.

CM Punk, Edge, Seth Rollins, Liv Morgan, and Iyo Sky are among the best to win the annual high-stakes matchup; not everyone can achieve the success they did.

Ahead of the October 10 return of the Money in the Bank premium live event, emanating from New Orleans, these are the competitors for whom acquiring the most coveted briefcase in professional wrestling did not net the expected stardom.

It appeared as though the stars had aligned and one of the most intriguing new faces in WWE in the mid-2000s was on his way to superstardom when Mr. Kennedy scaled the ladder and retrieved the Money in the Bank briefcase at WrestleMania 23.

Cocky, confident, and a great talker, he had captured the attention of the fans and had some thinking he was the next big thing in professional wrestling.

He may have been, but a perceived injury forced him to the sidelines, and WWE called an audible, with Kennedy dropping the briefcase to Edge, who would become the first Superstar to ever successfully cash in two of them.

During an interview with NBC Boston's Steve Fall , Kennedy noted that the triceps injury that kept him out was a misdiagnosis, one that altered the course of his wrestling career.

Realistically, there was probably a window on Sandow and how far he was going to go in WWE.

He was incredibly popular with the audience under his "Damien Mizdow" persona and his willingness to mimic WWE's past and present Superstars each week. Still, there was only so far that was going to take him, regardless of how warmly accepted his 2013 Money in the Bank victory was.

Booking never really gave him much of a chance, either.

Shortly after John Cena returned from injury in October 2013, Sandow cashed in his title opportunity by telling the babyface he would, then lost a competitive match in which the champion put him over as a threat, but little more.

What should have been a bigger moment for Sandow, one that would have better justified his loss, was instead a forgettable loss that would doom him to midcard status the remainder of his WWE run.

The year 2020 was a fever dream for most, especially in WWE, where the global pandemic forced significant changes, including the format of that year's Money in the Bank premium live event.

Not held in the Thunderdome where the rest of the shows were, the event's namesake matches took place in WWE Headquarters, where the Superstars involved fought up several stories before grabbing the briefcase on the roof of the iconic building.

Not only was Otis' title shot doomed to failure because he was nowhere near ready at that point, but he was also not a believable main-event star despite his popularity among fans.

The finish did not help matters, either.

Otis did not so much as climb the ladder to win the match as he simply lucked into it, catching the briefcase as AJ Styles fumbled it directly into his arms.

By the time October rolled around, it had become evident that Otis was not the guy the company needed at that point and he lost the briefcase to The Miz at the October Hell in a Cell PLE.

He has been a midcard mainstay since, but is one of the most beloved stars on the roster, if the audience's reaction to him is any indication.

If there was ever a Superstar whose run with the Money in the Bank briefcase felt sabotaged, it was Austin Theory's.

The winner of the 2022 match, he was in the midst of a big push and very much felt like a Superstar ready to have the rocket strapped to his back and to be pushed to the moon.

Then creative regimes changed, and so did Theory's trajectory.

On the November 7, 2022, episode of Raw, the young Atlantean cashed in his guaranteed championship opportunity...on the United States Championship.

A young star who had previously shared the same ring with "Stone Cold" Steve Austin, Vince McMahon, and Pat McAfee at WrestleMania 38 had just lost his opportunity to become a main event star in a match for a secondary title.

It was a massive letdown for Theory, but not for the fans who believed he was not ready for that position in the first place.

He would bounce back and beat John Cena at WrestleMania the following year, but he never returned to the heights he was at when he first captured the briefcase. Within a year, he would be tagging with Grayson Waller and losing more than he won.

His arrival in The Vision was a nice step up, but he is still clearly not valued as a main event star, fairly or not.

articles.title: Why did AJ Styles return after retirement? WWE Hall of Famer makes emotional comeback to the ring after 246 days following Gunther loss
articles.summary: WWE Hall of Famer AJ Styles shocked wrestling fans by returning to the ring after his retirement to save his son, Avery Styles.
articles.body: WWE Hall of Famer AJ Styles shocked wrestling fans by returning to the ring after his retirement to save his son, Avery Styles. The emotional moment happened at Atlanta Wrestling Entertainment, where Avery was attacked following his match against GWC Jr. Champion Tristan Moody. AJ rushed into the ring and fought off Moody’s allies before helping his son to his feet.Styles had retired from professional wrestling earlier this year after losing to Gunther at WWE Royal Rumble 2026. He was later inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame and moved into a backstage role.Why did AJ Styles come back after retiring from WWE?Avery Styles was competing at an Atlanta Wrestling Entertainment event when things quickly turned ugly. He faced GWC Jr. Champion Tristan Moody in a match for the title. Avery won the match by disqualification after one of Moody’s allies pushed him off the top rope.The situation became even worse after the match. More of Moody’s allies entered the ring and attacked Avery. With his son surrounded, AJ Styles suddenly appeared.The WWE Hall of Famer immediately stepped into the ring and started fighting off the attackers. Styles even attempted to hit a Styles Clash, but his move was stopped when one of the opponents was pulled away.Once the ring was cleared, AJ helped Avery back to his feet. The father and son then shared an emotional moment inside the ring.The appearance was surprising because Styles had already announced his retirement from in-ring competition. He faced Gunther at the Royal Rumble in January 2026 and lost the match. Styles then stepped away from wrestling and was later announced as part of the 2026 WWE Hall of Fame class.He has since taken on a different role in WWE. Styles has worked as a scout and has also been involved in coaching at the WWE Performance Center.However, AJ had previously admitted that there was one situation that could potentially bring him back. Speaking on The AJ Styles Show, he explained that wrestling alongside his sons could be meaningful enough to change his mind.“How long is it going to take my son, or sons, to get into a position where I’m able to do the show with them that matters? If it doesn’t matter…I’ll be honest with you, I’m probably not going to come back for an indie show, even if it’s to wrestle my boys. I’m probably not doing that. I don’t mind being a special guest like a manager, but if I do come back, hopefully I’m not 60 and it’s on a big show. What father wouldn’t want to come back and tag with his sons? I don’t know if that opportunity will come because it depends on how long it’s going to take,” Styles said.That makes his latest appearance even more interesting.Styles did not return for a scheduled match. He returned because his son was in trouble. articles.title: Lionel Messi to join Argentina for farewell match against Benin
articles.summary: The friendly marks a symbolic passing of the torch for a player whose international legacy includes a World Cup title.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi will bring the curtain down on his glittering Argentina career with a farewell friendly against Benin that marks the dawn of a new era for the South American champions.

After more than two decades of service to his country, the 39-year-old superstar will hand over the captain’s armband for good as he makes his final appearance in the Albiceleste jersey on Tuesday at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.

Messi will be joined for his international swansong by 85,000 spectators and several of the teammates with whom he reached the pinnacle of football at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar , alongside members of Argentina’s emerging generation.

The friendly marks a symbolic passing of the torch for a player whose international legacy includes a World Cup title, two Copa America crowns and the Finalissima.

Messi will also bow out as Argentina’s record appearance-maker and leading scorer with 125 goals in 207 games as well as a record 68 assists.

His farewell comes two and a half months after Argentina’s ill-tempered World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey, where Messi exited in tears after making little impression.

“I gave it my all. I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance,” Messi wrote when announcing his international retirement in August.

Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028 although after the death of his father , Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated.

Members of Argentina’s 2022 World Cup-winning squad and their families will join Messi for Tuesday’s farewell against Benin, ranked 93rd in the world.

Veterans of that Doha triumph, such as Angel Di Maria, who retired from international football in 2024, will be there to witness the passing of the torch to a new generation charged with extending the Albiceleste’s golden era.

Several of the newcomers, including Franco Mastantuono and Leonel Flores, were not even born when “La Pulga” (“The Flea”) made his Argentina debut in 2005 for a team whose history had for so long been dominated by Diego Maradona.

“It’s going to be an unforgettable day for everyone. Everyone wants to be at this match, and now it’s just about enjoying it,” Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said.

Argentina’s new generation has already shown what it can do without its captain although nobody is pretending that replacing a man regarded by many as the greatest footballer in history will be straightforward.

“Collectively, we will try to fill the void left by Leo,” said Scaloni, who is negotiating a contract extension after leaving his future unresolved following the World Cup defeat in July.

Scaloni, who mastered the art of building the right supporting cast around Messi, will also say goodbye on Tuesday to 38-year-old vice captain Nicolas Otamendi.

Like Messi and Otamendi, midfielders Rodrigo De Paul and Giovani Lo Celso were called up solely for the Benin game, raising the possibility that neither will represent Argentina again.

Those certain to be involved, at least from the bench, include other veterans of the 2022 World Cup who will be the standard-bearers for Argentina after Messi: defender Cristian Romero, midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernandez, and forwards Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez.

Tenacious centre back Romero is set to inherit the captain’s armband, first worn by Messi at the 2010 World Cup in South Africa.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez and Lautaro Martinez are next in the captain hierarchy.

They have already begun to rally around Messi’s heirs, who showed their appetite for success in Argentina’s first game since the World Cup final, against Bolivia in Cordoba on Wednesday.

Argentina swept the Bolivians aside 4-0 with young talents Nico Paz and Jose Manuel Lopez among the scorers.

They followed that victory with a 7-0 rout of Burkina Faso at the Monumental on Saturday with Mastantuono and Gianluca Prestianni scoring their first international goals.

While Argentina’s future is beginning to take shape, one small but symbolically significant question remains: Who will inherit Messi’s number 10 shirt ?

“We won’t give the number 10 to anyone until Leo’s match takes place,” Scaloni said. “After that, we’ll see.”

articles.title: La polémica revelación sobre Jhon Durán que destapó su excompañero Fred: "Ya soy rico, no necesito correr"
articles.standfirst: Fred revela la insólita respuesta de Jhon Durán para no entrenar en Turquía
articles.summary: Fred revela la insólita respuesta de Jhon Durán para no entrenar en Turquía
articles.body: El delantero colombiano Jhon Jáder Durán vuelve a acaparar los reflectores en el fútbol internacional, aunque esta vez no por sus anotaciones. El mediocampista brasileño Fred (exjugador del Manchester United) reveló intimidades del vestuario durante su etapa compartida en el Fenerbahçe de Turquía, exponiendo particulares detalles sobre la actitud del atacante cafetero durante los entrenamientos. En declaraciones recientes para Charla Podcast, Fred recordó las charlas que solía tener con el delantero para motivarlo a exigirse en la preparación física diaria: "Ese tipo no le importa nada, amigo, ¡qué tipo tan divertido! Es una gran persona. Pero, sabes, no le importa nada. Cuando estábamos de juerga, le decía: 'Vamos, Durán, hagamos entrenamiento, corramos un poco por ahí'", le decía el brasileño. La respuesta del colombiano era tajante: "Hermano, ya soy rico, no necesito correr en absoluto". Según el relato de Fred, tras dar esa contestación, Durán solía marcharse directamente al departamento médico del club. El mediocampista aclaró que no se trató de algo puntual, sino de una conducta progresiva: "Cuando llegó por primera vez al Fenerbahçe, al menos salía a los entrenamientos y eso, pero después lo dejó todo por completo, lo abandonó". Fred también revivió la conversación que mantuvieron cuando se negociaba la salida de Durán rumbo al Zenit de Rusia. Al comentarle que con el nuevo movimiento ganaría todavía más dinero, el delantero respondió: "Hermano, cuanto más, mejor, cuanto más, mejor. Ya he salvado completamente la vida mía, de mi familia y de tres generaciones después de mí". Esta estabilidad económica proviene del multimillonario contrato que firmó tras su traspaso desde el Aston Villa al Al Nassr de Arabia Saudita, en una operación que superó los 70 millones de euros. A pesar de sus revelaciones sobre la disciplina en las prácticas, Fred enfatizó que guarda un buen concepto personal del atacante colombiano, describiéndolo como "una buena persona y muy bromista", descartando así cualquier fricción personal grave dentro del plantel. Actualmente, tras su paso por el fútbol turco y un breve período en el Zenit ruso, Durán milita en el Benfica de Portugal en condición de préstamo, manteniéndose como ficha del Al Nassr.
